# FallForge

> The forge for sovereign AI, two ways in. (1) Mint an owned small model for one repetitive task — proven against its baseline by a deterministic gate with a signed receipt, beats-your-baseline-or-you-don't-pay, running on your own hardware. (2) The AI concierge installer for FallHub: auto-detects a small business's vertical from its website, harvests the footprint into a grounding kernel, packages a FallHub deployment, pre-configures the LLM router across five cost/quality blends, and hands the buyer a working AI-first operating system. Sovereign AI you own and can prove, not rent. Published by AI-Native Solutions. MIT. ◊·κ=1.

## Mint an owned model (own the AI you're renting)

Bring one repetitive task (triage, classification, extraction, routing) and a few example inputs with correct answers. FallForge mints a small model specialised to that task, measures it against its baseline on a held-out set with a deterministic gate, and issues a signed receipt (beats baseline by X%, this much cheaper/faster — the gate can and does return LOSES). You own the model file and run it private. Free proof node for one task, then a fixed per-node fee, or a monthly retainer to run and re-mint it. Regulated work (legal/tax/medical/financial) is off the menu, counsel first. The whole factory is live and mutation-gated: the gate, the mint (fallforge-mint), the runtime (fallnode), the catalogue, the mesh, and fallforge-factory. Contact: mailto:sjgant80@gmail.com. Page: /mint.html.

## What it is (the installer)

FallForge turns "install your business OS" from a technical exercise into a 20-minute AI-driven concierge. The buyer answers three questions (business name, URL, vertical override) and watches five phases execute:

1. Discover — fetch website + signal pages · extract text, links, socials
2. Kernel distil — LLM populates the vertical's kernel.json schema
3. Wire — assemble ZIP with kernel + BOM + install guide + module list · optional GitHub push
4. Calibrate — autopilot tuning on the deployed instance
5. Handoff — final report + live URLs

## Supported verticals (auto-detected)

- Hospitality (holiday rental, glamping, B&B, boutique hotel)
- Trades (plumber, electrician, decorator, gas engineer)
- Ad firm (creative agency, brand studio, freelance strategy)
- Accounting practice (bookkeeper, VAT, self-assessment)
- Barbershop chain (multi-location grooming, extensible to gyms/cafés/salons)

## Router blends baked into every install

- Full Frontier — Claude Opus 4.8 across all phases (£80–£300/mo)
- 80/20 default — Claude reasoning + Groq Llama bulk (£20–£60/mo)
- 50/50 — Balanced (£8–£25/mo)
- Full Open — Groq Llama 3.3 70B (£4–£12/mo)
- Local only — WebLLM Llama 3.1 8B in browser (£0/mo)

## Install modes

- Local (£0) — runs entirely in browser · BYOK · sovereign
- Hosted (£29 one-off) — Cloudflare Worker for CORS-free fetching + deeper crawls
- Pro concierge (£199 one-off) — human review of the FallForge output + calibration
